title: Rematch: Jett Marrows
summary: Jett Marrows has chalked a full circuit on the salt flats and told the whole moorage you're scared of flat ground. Three laps around Saltmouth's beacons — east gate, dune overlook, water tower, old salt pan — boost, drift, and absolutely no canyon to blame. The purse is real; the trash talk started yesterday.

objectives.label: Stage at the moorage mast — the chalk start line
Lap one: east gate → overlook → water tower → salt pan
Lap two — Jett always shows his line here
Final lap — finish across the moorage chalk line

offer.text: Parcel! You lucked out in the canyon — slick glass, no witnesses, asterisk pending. So I've drawn you a REAL test: three laps, flat salt, four beacons, nowhere to hide. Purse is four hundred and twenty of my actual credits, because I enjoy theatre.

He's been chalking that start line since dawn and re-chalking it every time the wind argues. Take his money, kid. Flat circuits are about exit speed and nerve — you've been renting both off me for months.
Rules: pass every gate, keep it above ground, and if your weird crate hums the lap times back at me, that's BETWEEN you and the clergy.

accept.text: She accepts! Listen for my horn at the overlook — it's how I say 'this is where you lost'. Free lesson, rookie: brake BEFORE the water tower's shadow, not inside it. That one's just good manners.

Race notes: the pan gate is the money gate. Enter wide, drift the whole crust, boost out flat, and do NOT chase Jett into lap two — he always over-cooks the tower turn showing off. Let him gift-wrap it.
Copy. Three laps, four gates, one scheduled over-cooking. If I win, the asterisk on his record gets a little friend.

complete.text: …The tower turn. The ONE turn. I made eye contact with my own reflection in the tank and the next thing I knew you were a rumour on the horizon. Fine. FINE. Purse is yours. Theatre's expensive.

For the record, rook— Varga. That's the fastest anyone's lapped the flats since Davenant stopped answering the band. I'm not saying it's a pattern. The asterisk is saying it. Quietly. I'll have it killed.

Nice exits, kid. Driftline nets are calling it 'the moorage chalk massacre' — theatre, like the man said. Word's out there's a second rider out there chalking lines at the Drowned Array. Doesn't talk. Just chalks. When you're ready.
